propositions: Command syntax is currently fragmented across reusable argparse parsers, imperative argv loops, hand-maintained help files, and curated descriptions, causing drift between parser, runtime help, and documentation.
All command grammars must be produced by a single runtime-used side-effect-free argparse factory with no duplicate parsers, regex-based grammars, or alternative parser frameworks.
Generated package help and grouped overview must be byte-current and derived deterministically from factories, serving before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
Parser migrations must maintain argv acceptance/rejection parity, diagnostic output, stream handling, and exit codes compared to production behavior.
Top-level routing must recognize only global config tokens, command identity, first-token help forms, and unknown commands, with nested parsing delegated to handler factories.
Exact command aliases reuse canonical artifacts via compatibility shims, while retired/hidden commands remain undiscoverable or resolved only for explicit help.
